subject: inla failing with prediction of big dataset

messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: inla failing with prediction of big dataset
parts:
I've got an SPDE model with 19,000 observations. I'm trying to predict it onto a grid with 90,000 points. It takes about 6-8 hours to run. The model runs to completion without error, but it is failing to predict onto the entire grid -- it's done this a few times, and it varies where the model fails.

The first map is from ggplot2 and the second is from ArcGIS, just to see if it was a drawing problem rather than a computation problem.

I suppose I don't need 90,000 points, but I want a dense enough grid that I can interpolate a nice, smooth surface.

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla failing with prediction of big dataset
parts:
What is your posterior range?

It looks like the prediction is regressing to zero in the south. This is supposed to happen when you move away from the data. Where distance is measured "in spatial ranges".

By the way, if you are using prediction stacks, you may want to use inla.posterior.sample instead.

Haakon

I find it possible that the algorithm failed. Can you send me the summary(result) and result$logfile?
Use "cat" to write to .txt files, and attach to email.

The result is very strange with that data, right? There could be a coding error also.

Haakon
